<!-- lead -->
For hospital and clinic IT teams deploying MIA Toolkit. MIA Toolkit is a free, open-source (MIT), **offline** desktop application that consolidates a patient's imaging media (CDs, USB folders, ZIP downloads) into one DICOMDIR archive (the standard DICOM media file-set) on a USB drive. Its only network call is the user-initiated update check described below; it makes **no network calls** otherwise.

<!-- body -->
## System requirements

| | Minimum |
|---|---|
| **macOS** | macOS 12 or newer (`LSMinimumSystemVersion` 12.0) |
| **Windows** | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x64; also installs on Windows 11 on ARM, running under x64 emulation) |
| Disk | Free space sufficient for the imaging media being consolidated |
| Network | None required (download only) |

## Install model

### Windows (Inno Setup installer `MIA-Toolkit-Setup-<ver>.exe`)

The installer is configured with `PrivilegesRequired=lowest` and `PrivilegesRequiredOverridesAllowed=dialog`. That gives two install modes:

| Mode | How it is chosen | Default folder | Start-menu shortcut | Uninstall registration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Per-user (default)** | default; or `/CURRENTUSER` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MIA Toolkit` | current user's Start menu | `HKCU` |
| **All users (machine-wide)** | "Install for all users" in the install-mode dialog (needs admin / UAC); or `/ALLUSERS` | see caveat below | all-users Start menu | `HKLM` |

- Per-user mode needs **no administrator rights** and makes no machine-wide changes.
- Per the Inno Setup documentation, allowing `dialog` automatically allows the `/ALLUSERS` and `/CURRENTUSER` command-line switches, and using either one skips the dialog.<sup>†</sup>
- **Caveat for machine-wide installs:** the default folder is defined with `{localappdata}`, which is a per-user location even in all-users mode. An `/ALLUSERS` install therefore defaults into the *installing admin's* `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` unless you pass `/DIR`. For a machine-wide install, always pass `/DIR="C:\Program Files\MIA Toolkit"`.<sup>†</sup>
- Upgrades install in place: the installer has a fixed `AppId`, so a newer version replaces the old one in the same folder and mode.
- There is no MSI. For Intune, wrap the `.exe` as a Win32 app (`.intunewin`) and use the command lines below; choose the **User** install context for per-user mode or **System** for `/ALLUSERS`.<sup>†</sup>

### macOS (`MIA-Toolkit-<ver>.dmg`)

The app ships as a signed and notarized `.app` inside a `.dmg`. Copy `MIA Toolkit.app` into `/Applications` (machine-wide) or `~/Applications` (per-user). There is no installer, licensing agent, server enrolment or activation step.

## Silent / unattended install

### Windows

```powershell
# Per-user, fully silent (run in the user's context):
MIA-Toolkit-Setup-<ver>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /CURRENTUSER

# Machine-wide, fully silent (run elevated / as SYSTEM):
MIA-Toolkit-Setup-<ver>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /ALLUSERS /DIR="C:\Program Files\MIA Toolkit"

# Useful extras:
#   /SILENT              progress window only, instead of /VERYSILENT
#   /LOG="C:\path.log"   write an install log
#   /TASKS="desktopicon" also create a desktop shortcut (off by default)
```

- A silent install does **not** launch the app afterwards (the post-install launch is skipped in silent mode).
- `/CURRENTUSER` + `/VERYSILENT` + `/DIR=` is exactly what our release pipeline runs on a Windows build machine before each release is published (see "Post-install check"). The `/ALLUSERS` line is not yet tested by us on Windows<sup>†</sup>.

### macOS

```bash
# Mount, copy to /Applications, detach:
hdiutil attach MIA-Toolkit-<ver>.dmg -nobrowse -readonly -mountpoint /tmp/mia-dmg
ditto "/tmp/mia-dmg/MIA Toolkit.app" "/Applications/MIA Toolkit.app"
hdiutil detach /tmp/mia-dmg
```

**MDM (Jamf, Intune, Kandji, Mosyle):**

- Deploy the `.dmg` through your MDM's DMG/app workflow, or build a component package from the notarized app and push that: `pkgbuild --component "/tmp/mia-dmg/MIA Toolkit.app" --install-location /Applications MIA-Toolkit-<ver>.pkg`
- That `.pkg` is **not signed** by us (we have no Developer ID *Installer* certificate). Some MDM workflows require a signed package (Intune's macOS LOB app type, for example). Sign it with your organisation's installer certificate, or use your MDM's DMG / unmanaged-PKG route. *(verify with your MDM)*
- The app bundle itself stays signed by our Developer ID and notarized by Apple whichever way you wrap it.
- **Air-gapped Macs:** the notarization ticket is stapled to the `.dmg`, not to the `.app` inside it (checked on v0.1.13 with `xcrun stapler validate`). On a Mac with internet access Gatekeeper confirms notarization online. Apps placed by an MDM normally carry no quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper does not assess them on first launch. If a fully offline Mac shows a Gatekeeper prompt for an app copied by hand from the DMG, deploy through the MDM or contact us.

## Post-install check (headless)

Releases after v0.1.13 have headless flags (v0.1.13's `--selftest` performs an import check only) that open no window and make no network call:

- `--version` prints the installed version.
- `--selftest` imports the whole bundle, builds a DICOMDIR from a tiny synthetic DICOM study in a temporary folder, deletes it, prints one result line and exits `0` (pass) or `1` (fail).

```bash
# macOS
"/Applications/MIA Toolkit.app/Contents/MacOS/mia" --selftest
```

```powershell
# Windows (a windowed app, so read the result from the report file + exit code)
$env:MIA_SELFTEST_REPORT = "$env:TEMP\mia-selftest.txt"
(Start-Process "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\MIA Toolkit\MIA Toolkit.exe" -ArgumentList --selftest -Wait -PassThru).ExitCode
Get-Content "$env:TEMP\mia-selftest.txt"
```

## Network, proxy, and firewall

MIA Toolkit makes **no background network calls**. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no account, no cloud sync, and no automatic update check. The app's single network call is the **user-initiated "Check for Updates"** (one HTTPS GET of `https://miatools.tech/version.json`, see Update policy). Other outbound connections are **standard links the user explicitly clicks** (e.g. the website or support email), which open in the user's default browser or mail client — not from the app.

- **Nothing to allowlist.** No domains, ports, or endpoints need to be opened for the app to function. Allow `miatools.tech` (HTTPS/443) only if you want users to be able to run the update check.
- The app works fully on an **air-gapped / fully isolated** workstation.

## Data locations

| Data | Location |
|---|---|
| Working project (copied disc contents, inventory, archive build, session logs) | `~/Documents/MedicalArchive` by default (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\MedicalArchive`); the user can choose another folder |
| Delivered archive | the USB drive or folder the user picks at the end |
| App settings (only the interface language) | **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\mia-toolkit\config.json` · **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/mia-toolkit/config.json` |
| Program files | Windows: the install folder above · macOS: the `.app` bundle |

- The app does not write to the registry beyond the installer's own uninstall entry, and it has no machine-wide settings or policy file.
- The default project path is built from the user's home folder (`~/Documents`), not from the Windows "Documents" known-folder API. If your policy redirects Documents (e.g. OneDrive Known Folder Move), the default may not follow the redirect. Users can pick a different folder.<sup>†</sup>
- Imaging media (PHI) is read from the source discs or folders and written only to local disk and the destination USB drive. It never leaves the workstation.

## Update policy

- **No auto-update.** The app never checks for or downloads updates on its own.
- **IT controls versions.** New versions are published on GitHub Releases. IT decides when to test and roll out a version, using the same silent-install commands above (in-place upgrade). You can pin a validated version indefinitely.

> **Update check (user-initiated only):** the Help/app menu's "Check for Updates" performs a single HTTPS GET of a static version file (`https://miatools.tech/version.json`) **only when a user clicks it**. It uses a generic User-Agent with no version, no query parameters, no identifiers and no background checks, ever. It only reports whether a newer version exists; it never downloads or installs anything. Blocking that domain disables the check cleanly with no other effect on the app.

## Code signing and verification

- **macOS:** signed (Apple Developer ID) and notarized since v0.1.5. Verify with `spctl --assess --type execute -vv "/Applications/MIA Toolkit.app"` (expect `source=Notarized Developer ID`).
- **Windows:** the installer is **not yet code-signed**. SmartScreen may show "Unknown publisher": choose More info → Run anyway, or allow it via your endpoint policy (e.g. by file hash). An Authenticode certificate is planned; this section will be updated when signed installers ship.
- **Checksums:** the SHA-256 of each installer is published in `https://miatools.tech/version.json`. Releases after v0.1.13 also attach a `SHA256SUMS` file (`shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`, or `Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows).
- **Provenance + SBOM (releases after v0.1.13):** GitHub build-provenance attestations (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo Fritanga-Collective/mia-toolkit`) and one CycloneDX SBOM per platform (`*.cdx.json`).

## Uninstall

- **Windows:** Settings → Apps → MIA Toolkit → Uninstall, or run the uninstaller in the install folder silently: `"<install folder>\unins000.exe" /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART` (per-user default: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MIA Toolkit\unins000.exe`). The uninstall entry lives under `HKCU\...\Uninstall` (per-user) or `HKLM\...\Uninstall` (all users), key `{8F3A1C2E-7B4D-4E9A-9C1F-2D5E6A7B8C90}_is1`.<sup>†</sup>
- **macOS:** delete `MIA Toolkit.app` from `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`).
- **Residual data:** the uninstaller removes only program files. The settings file and any project under `~/Documents/MedicalArchive` stay until removed by hand. Delete them if a full wipe is required (the project folder can contain patient imaging).

## Support

We never need patient data. Send de-identified screenshots or logs only — never studies, DICOM files or PHI. Support is best-effort by email at **support@miatools.tech**, with a target first response within **2 business days**.
